PullRequest.Title: Sort chat pill dropdown entries newest first
PullRequest.Body:
Session artifacts and references are recorded by append, so their stored order runs oldest to newest. Every pill that lists them now shows the most recent entry at the top of its group:

- **Artifacts / References** — `readSessionArtifactsNewestFirst` feeds both the workbench Agent Host pills and the Agents Window partition, so each dropdown section (Pull Requests, Issues, Commits, Websites, Files, Resources, Images) opens on what the session recorded last.
- **Pull Requests / Issues** — the promoted GitHub links are newest first too. The pull requests the session recorded now lead the ones discovered from its GitHub state on *both* surfaces (they previously disagreed), which also makes the session's latest pull request its active one — consistent with `withMostRecentSessionPullRequest`, which already treats "most recent" as the main pull request.
- **Browsers** — the most recently opened browser is listed first.
- **Subagents** — the most recently started subagent is listed first.

The Customizations pill is deliberately unchanged: it is a catalog grouped by kind rather than a recency stream.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The complexity change, both reactive call paths, event sources, and map lifecycle are directly visible in repository code. Exact user-visible magnitude depends on how many browser views a session accumulates, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: JavaScript array element moves and temporary allocation on the renderer/UI thread
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each recomputation still scans all n known browser views, but `unshift` additionally moves every previously matched element, making construction O(n + m²) for m matching agent-owned views instead of O(n). The helper is used by both pill surfaces and recomputes on browser-set and label events (title, favicon, loading-state, and navigation changes).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased UI-thread CPU/GC pressure and pill update latency, potentially causing visible jank in long-running agent sessions with many browser views
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Both call sites built their matching browser list with `filter` or `push`, preserving an O(n) scan of the known-browser map on each reactive update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The shared newest-first helper inserts every match at index zero, shifting the accumulated array for each matching browser on every recomputation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side line 113 replaces the prior callers' append/filter construction with `views.unshift(input)`, introducing repeated shifting proportional to the number of already matched views.
Findings.Title: Build newest-first browser lists without quadratic front insertion
Findings.Impact: When an agent session accumulates many browser pages, each page load/navigation emits several label events; both pill surfaces can repeatedly perform quadratic array copying before updating the UI, delaying rendering and increasing GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: `getAgentBrowserViewsNewestFirst` iterates the complete `getKnownBrowserViews()` map and executes `views.unshift(input)` for every matching owner. `SessionBrowsersControl` and `AgentHostSessionInputPills` both call it from derived UI state, and both register every browser input's `onDidChangeLabel`; `BrowserEditorInput` fires that event for title, favicon, loading-state, navigation, model resolution, and explicit navigation changes. The known-view map has no cardinality cap and removes entries only when an input is disposed.
Findings.Recommendation: Append matching inputs with `push` during the map walk and call `views.reverse()` once afterward; this preserves newest-first ordering and restores O(n) construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser pill updates in the workbench and Agents Window while an agent session owns multiple integrated-browser pages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser-set changes and BrowserEditorInput label events synchronously invalidate derived pill state; filtering/reordering and entry construction must complete on the UI thread before the pill can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: n known browser views in the window and m views owned by the active session/chat (including direct subagents); no fixed cap was found, and entries persist until their BrowserEditorInput is disposed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized on the renderer/UI event path. Both pill surfaces independently subscribe and recompute; there is no batching or coalescing across title, favicon, loading-state, navigation, or browser-set events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache serves the reordered list. Every invalidation rescans the current map and rebuilds a fresh array; warm and cold behavior are therefore the same aside from model availability.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added `unshift` produces O(n + m²) array movement, both call paths and their event sources are directly traced, and prior construction was O(n).
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical sessions may have only a few browsers, but long-running browser-heavy agent sessions can accumulate enough views, and each navigation produces multiple label events. Exact frame-time impact is unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity CPU/GC regression. Use append plus one final reverse to preserve newest-first order in linear time.

Scenarios.Scenario: Artifact, reference, pull-request, and issue pill metadata refresh when session metadata changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session metadata is synchronously parsed, partitioned, deduplicated, and grouped before pill state can update; all work is local CPU/allocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of artifact/reference records and related GitHub links in one session after deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous derived-state recomputation; no parallelism or external work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each metadata change rebuilds parsed arrays and sets. The new reversal is one linear pass; no cache behavior or invalidation semantics changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed helpers and their consumers were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact histories can grow, but the diff adds only bounded O(a) copying/reversal and does not change external polling cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: newest-first ordering adds linear local work and retains no additional long-lived state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents Window session-list GitHub promotion and artifact presentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On session metadata updates, artifacts are partitioned and GitHub references are prepared synchronously before observable session data updates. Existing GitHub polling occurs downstream, but the diff only reorders the same deduplicated URLs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of session artifacts plus discovered pull requests/issues; effective external cardinality remains the same after deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local partitioning is synchronous. No changed limiter, fan-out, or scheduling behavior was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Partition arrays are rebuilt per metadata update; reversing the three local arrays is linear. Existing pull-request presentation/cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: partition and promotion call paths were inspected and no boundary was added or moved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream GitHub latency is outside the changed mechanism; URL order changes which PR is active but not request count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the diff does not increase network cardinality or add blocking boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Subagent pill refresh as chats are appended or their titles/statuses change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active session chat array is synchronously filtered, mapped, and reversed before rendering the subagent section.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in the active session and direct subagents of the selected parent chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable recomputation with no external calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A fresh filtered/mapped array was already built; the added in-place reverse operates on that temporary array and adds one linear pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed collection pipeline and ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large chat histories increase all existing collection work, but the added reversal remains linear and bounded by the already-materialized result.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no mutation of authoritative state, retained memory, or superlinear work is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced browser-pill reactive updates, artifact/GitHub metadata processing, session-list presentation, and subagent rendering. Submitted one medium-severity repeated-work finding for quadratic front insertion; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was introduced or moved onto a critical path.
